text: Split node by the highest differing bit.

A cat tree (猫树) answers static range queries in O(1) for any associative merge whose partial results can be precomputed. Build a segment tree over a power-of-two length. At each node with midpoint mid, store the answer for every suffix [i, mid] of the left half and every prefix [mid + 1, j] of the right half. A query [l, r] with l ≠ r uses the node where l and r are first split, which is found from the highest differing bit of l and r.

O(n log n) memory and preprocessing, O(1) per query, no LCA walk. For maximum subarray sum each stored entry holds the best inside, the best touching the middle, and the sum. Knapsack-like merges (好吃的题目 P6240) store a whole DP array per position, so queries cost the merge of two arrays.
Maximum subarray sum on random ranges, checked against trying every subarray in Python. The highest bit where l and r differ tells the depth of their split node directly: no tree walk at all.
Tags (add, max prefix of adds).

Historic maximum (区间历史最值): besides the current values ai, ask for max over time of ai. With range add, each node keeps mx (current max) and hmx (historic max), and two lazy tags: add (total pending addition) and hadd (the largest prefix of that pending sequence of additions). When pushing tags (add, hadd) onto a child: child.hmx = max(child.hmx, child.mx + hadd), child.hadd = max(child.hadd, child.add + hadd), then child.mx += add, child.add += add.

The order matters: the historic values must be updated with the child's old current values before adding. That "max prefix of pending additions" tag is the whole trick; CPU 监控(P4314) adds assignment tags the same way, and P6242 combines it with chmin (NOI 篇第5章).
Random range adds (positive and negative), current maxima and historic maxima, checked against tracking every element's best value in Python.
Two Fenwick trees per centroid.

Dynamic centroid decomposition with code (拓展篇第27章 gave the idea): query "sum of values within distance k of x" with point updates (震波 P6329). For each centroid c keep two Fenwick trees indexed by distance: Fc[d] = total value at distance d from c inside c's piece, and Gc[d] = total value inside c's piece at distance d from c's centroid parent.

Query(x, k): start with Fx up to k; then for each centroid ancestor p of the current c: add Fp up to k − dist(x, p), and subtract Gc up to k − dist(x, p) (those vertices were already counted below). Update changes O(log n) Fenwick entries the same way. dist uses the original tree (LCA).

title: 莫队二次离线与 Top Tree

text: Prefix contributions offline; top trees in brief.

Second-offline Mo (莫队二次离线): when moving a Mo pointer costs O(log n) (e.g. "count pairs i < j in the window with ai > aj", 莫队二次离线 P4887), write each pointer move's contribution as f(prefix, x): "the effect of element x against the prefix 1 … p". Record all those (p, x-range) requests offline, sweep p from 1 to n once with a structure that makes each request O(1), and add the results back. Total O(n√n) instead of O(n√n log n).

Top trees (Top Tree) maintain path and subtree information on a dynamic forest at once, generalising LCT (拓展篇第14章); they are almost never required in contests: LCT plus "virtual subtree" sums (keeping the sum of non-preferred children) covers subtree queries in practice.

title: zkw 线段树与线段树分裂

text: Bottom-up loops; move nodes into a new tree.

zkw segment tree (zkw 线段树 , bottom-up): put the leaves at positions M + i where M is a power of two ≥ n + 2, parents at i / 2. A point update walks up with p >>= 1. A range query [l, r] starts from the open ends l − 1 and r + 1 and moves both up until they become siblings, adding the sibling subtrees they pass.

No recursion, so it is several times faster than the usual segment tree, and about 10 lines. Range updates with lazy tags are possible but awkward; use it for point update + range query (or range update + point query).

Segment tree splitting (线段树分裂) is the reverse of merging (拓展篇): to move the values in [x, y] out of a dynamic (value-indexed) segment tree into a new tree, walk down both at once. A node fully inside [x, y] is moved by pointer, not copied; partially covered nodes are split into a new node for each side. Each split creates O(log n) nodes.

With merge and split together, sets of values can be cut and glued freely: "move these values to a new set / merge set t into p / count / k-th" (P5494). Merging costs are paid by the nodes they remove, splits add O(log n), so the total stays O((n + q) log n).
The P5494 operations (0 split off [x, y] as a new set, 1 merge, 2 add copies, 3 count in range, 4 k-th), run at random and checked against Python dictionaries of counts.
Segments in a set; split, assign, walk.

The Chtholly tree (珂朵莉树 , ODT, 颜色段均摊) stores the array as a set of maximal segments [l, r] with one value. split(pos) cuts the segment containing pos so that a new one starts at pos. Range assign = split(r + 1), split(l), erase everything between, insert one segment. Other operations just walk the segments in [l, r].

Fast only when random range assignments keep the number of segments small (expected O(n log log n) total, CF896C). Any operation that walks segments costs their count, so without assignments, or on adversarial data, it degrades to O(n) per operation. Always split(r + 1) before split(l): the other order can invalidate the first iterator.
